column1: admonish§Her father admonished her never to sign anything unread.§父亲**告诫**她，凡是没读过的东西绝不要签字。
adulate§Critics who adulate a first novel rarely help the second one.§一味**吹捧**处女作的评论家，很少帮得上第二部。
agonize§There is no point agonizing over a choice you cannot unmake.§为一个无法反悔的选择**苦苦纠结**毫无意义。
apostle§As an apostle of slow travel, he had not flown in nine years.§作为慢旅行的**倡导者**，他九年没坐过飞机。
assume§The map assumes a road that was closed twenty years ago.§这张地图**默认**存在一条二十年前就封闭的路。
blithe§She gave a blithe wave and disappeared into the crowd.§她**漫不经心**地挥了挥手，就消失在人群里。
bluff§The cottage stands on a bluff above the estuary.§那间小屋立在河口上方的**悬崖**上。
breed§Careless reporting breeds exactly the distrust it complains about.§粗率的报道恰恰**滋生**了它所抱怨的不信任。
chagrin§Much to her chagrin, the recording had not started.§让她十分**懊恼**的是，录音根本没开始。
cinematography§He studied cinematography by watching the same film forty times.§他靠把同一部电影看四十遍来学电影**摄影**。
clemency§Appeals for clemency arrived from three different countries.§来自三个国家的**求情**信陆续送到。
commensurate§Give the problem attention commensurate with its size.§给这个问题的关注，要与它的规模**相称**。
conciliate§He tried to conciliate both sides and satisfied neither.§他想**调和**双方，结果两边都不满意。
contaminate§Ash from the fire contaminated the water supply for a month.§大火产生的灰烬**污染**了水源一个月。
contempt§She held the whole procedure in open contempt.§她对整套程序公然表示**轻蔑**。
courageous§A courageous editor prints the correction on page one.§**有勇气**的编辑会把更正登在头版。
defect§Two engineers defected to a rival firm the same week.§两名工程师在同一周**投奔**了对手公司。
detriment§Cutting the survey short was to the detriment of the whole study.§缩短调查**损害**了整项研究。
dissemble§There was no point dissembling; the accounts spoke for themselves.§没必要**掩饰**，账目本身说明了一切。
draw§He drew the outline in four strokes and stopped.§他四笔就**画出**了轮廓，然后停了下来。
elucidate§Her footnotes elucidate a text that would otherwise defeat most readers.§她的脚注**阐明**了一部否则会难倒多数读者的文本。
emancipate§New machinery emancipated the workshop from the tides.§新机器把作坊从潮汐的限制中**解放**出来。
encapsulated§The batteries are encapsulated in resin to keep out damp.§电池被树脂**封装**起来以防潮。
enduring§The design proved enduring long after the company closed.§公司关门很久之后，这个设计依然**经久不衰**。
exasperate§Nothing exasperates a reader like an index with no page numbers.§没有比没有页码的索引更让读者**恼火**的了。
exonerate§Two years later a second inquiry exonerated the crew.§两年后的第二次调查**免除了船员的责任**。
extricate§He could not extricate himself from a promise made in public.§他无法从一个当众许下的承诺中**脱身**。
foment§The pamphlet fomented unrest in three neighboring towns.§这本小册子在三个邻镇**挑起**了骚动。
gallop§The story galloped through the office before lunch.§这个消息午饭前就在办公室里**飞快传开**了。
grudgingly§She grudgingly agreed to one more rehearsal.§她**勉强**同意再排练一次。
impertinent§The remark was impertinent as well as beside the point.§这句话既**无礼**，又离题。
implement§A stone implement found in the ditch dated the whole site.§沟里发现的一件石制**工具**确定了整个遗址的年代。
inadvertently§The footnote inadvertently gave away the ending.§这条脚注**无意**中泄露了结局。
ineluctable§Aging is ineluctable; decline is not.§衰老**无可避免**，衰退则未必。
inform§A short note informed us that the archive would close.§一张简短的便条**告知**我们档案馆将关闭。
informed§An informed guess beats an uninformed calculation.§**有依据**的猜测胜过无知的计算。
insuperable§What looked insuperable in June was routine by September.§六月看来**无法克服的**事，到九月已成常规。
interject§May I interject one date before you go on?§在你继续之前，我能**插一句**日期吗？
inveterate§An inveterate hoarder, he kept every ticket stub.§他是个**积习**难改的囤积者，每张票根都留着。
laity§The lecture was pitched at the laity and drew four hundred people.§这场讲座面向**外行**，吸引了四百人。
lash§Rain lashed the windows for most of the night.§雨大半夜都在**猛打**窗户。
make a case against§Nobody has made a serious case against the earlier dating.§还没人认真论证过**反对**更早的断代。
make a case for§The chapter makes a case for reading the letters in reverse.§这一章**论证了**应当倒着读这些信。
obligate§Nothing obligates you to answer a question you were not asked.§没有什么**强迫**你回答一个没人问你的问题。
pant§The dog panted in the shade and refused to move.§狗在阴凉处**喘着气**，怎么也不肯动。
patronize§They patronized the same bookshop for forty years.§他们**光顾**同一家书店四十年。
perturbation§News of the merger caused visible perturbation in the office.§合并的消息在办公室里引起了明显的**不安**。
plunge§She plunged into the archive and came out three years later.§她**一头扎进**档案里，三年后才出来。
postulate§Euclid's fifth postulate troubled mathematicians for centuries.§欧几里得第五**公设**困扰了数学家几个世纪。
predicate§The verb agrees with the subject, not with the predicate.§动词与主语一致，而不是与**谓语**一致。
preoccupation§His preoccupation with the deadline made him a poor listener.§他**一心惦记**截止日期，成了个糟糕的倾听者。
prone to§Small boats are prone to swamping in that channel.§小船在那条水道里**容易**进水。
provided§Provided the weather holds, the survey finishes on Friday.§**只要**天气不变，勘测周五就能完成。
putative§The putative benefits were never measured.§这些**声称的**好处从未被衡量过。
quench§A single cold spring quenched a whole village's thirst.§一眼冷泉**解了整个村子的渴**。
reciprocity§Reciprocity, not affection, kept the alliance alive.§维系这个联盟的是**互惠**，而非情谊。
refraction§Refraction through the ice split the beam into colors.§光线经冰**折射**后分成了彩色。
register§Please register the change before the end of the month.§请在月底前**登记**这项变更。
render§The delay rendered the whole schedule useless.§这次延误使整个进度表都**成了废纸**。
repute§A house of ill repute stood on the corner until 1920.§到一九二〇年为止，街角一直有一家**声名不佳**的房子。
rigid§He is rigid about method and generous about credit.§他在方法上**一板一眼**，在归功上却很大方。
saddle§She checked the saddle twice before letting the child ride.§让孩子骑之前，她把**马鞍**检查了两遍。
secularize§Once secularized, the building served as a grain store.§这座建筑**脱离宗教**用途后，改作了粮仓。
shift§He works the night shift and sleeps through the afternoon.§他上**夜班**，整个下午都在睡觉。
slacken§Do not slacken the rope until both feet are down.§双脚落地之前不要**放松**绳子。
staggering§A staggering number of letters survived the fire.§**数量惊人**的信件在火灾中幸存下来。
stymie§Bad weather stymied three attempts in a single week.§恶劣天气一周内**挫败**了三次尝试。
symposium§Her paper at the symposium was the shortest and the most quoted.§她在**研讨会**上的论文最短，却被引用最多。
tenant§Tenants organized before the landlord had finished the letter.§房东的信还没写完，**租户**们就已经组织起来了。
testament§The diary is a testament to how ordinary the year felt at the time.§这本日记**见证**了那一年在当时是多么平常。
tributary§For centuries the small state was a tributary of its neighbor.§几个世纪里，这个小国一直是邻国的**附庸**。
understate§To call the winter difficult is to understate it badly.§把那个冬天说成艰难，是严重的**轻描淡写**。
undue§He gave undue weight to a single interview.§他对一次访谈给予了**过分的重视**。
virtually§The two accounts are virtually identical.§这两份记述**几乎**完全一致。
vulgar§What one century calls vulgar the next puts in a museum.§一个世纪称之为**粗俗**的，下一个世纪把它放进博物馆。
warp§Prolonged heat can warp the record beyond playing.§长时间受热会使唱片**变形**到无法播放。
warrant§Officers arrived with a warrant early on Tuesday morning.§警官周二一早带着**搜查令**到达。
whim§The whole garden was laid out on the whim of one owner.§整座花园是按一位主人的**一时兴起**布置的。
wind ensemble§He wrote three pieces for wind ensemble and none for orchestra.§他为**管乐团**写了三首曲子，却没为管弦乐队写过一首。
woeful§The equipment was in woeful condition by the second winter.§到第二个冬天，设备的状况已经**糟糕透顶**。
